speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) presenting with behavioral changes and atypical focal neurological deficits.

This is an unusual presentation for SSPE given the rapid onset of focal weakness (1 week) vs. the slower cognitive decline (6 months), which more typically aligns with Hashimoto's Encephalopathy (HSE) or rapidly progressive dementia due to autoimmune encephalitis. I need to rule out metabolic causes and confirm antibody status.

REQUEST TEST: Antinuclear Antibody (ANA), Paraneoplastic Panel, and Brain MRI.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.
